title: Ossett's post-bargain line directly contradicts Bevan's own account of the same object. Ossett: 'better a stone that says something true than one that says nothing at all' (implies a standing, inscribed stone). Bevan, the actual stone-cutter, says in the same sequence of events: 'No stone either... lets the canvas fall back over the stone for good' (no stone stands at all). Two NPCs give mutually exclusive testimony about the same physical thing with no in-fiction excuse (neither is lying or misinformed by design).
where: The Pensioner's House (Ossett, 'tell him how the stone was decided') vs The Stone-Cutter's Lodge (Bevan, 'tell him no stone will stand here')
